nits: Pre-existing and unchanged by this PR: a method handler registered on a Mount's wildcard pattern (Route("/bar", ...) then Get("/bar/*", h)) is still not reported by Walk, because walk() recurses into SubRoutes and ignores that node's own handlers. Probe output is 'getStarOnMount [GET /bar/x]' on both HEAD and the PR, while GET /bar/zzz -> 200 from h. Worth a follow-up issue.

TestWalkRouteStubCollision has 13 cases; some (e.g. 'Route on root with Get inside only', 'Mount on a trailing-slash pattern skips bare stubs') are no-collision regression guards and could be named that way so the issue-specific cases are easier to spot.

report:
This PR is mergeable: I found nothing the contributor has to fix.

**Root cause.** The old `routes()` dropped a whole tree node whenever its `mSTUB` endpoint had a handler and the node had no subroutes. `Route("/bar")` leaves that stub marker on the `/bar` node permanently, so a `Get("/bar")` registered afterwards on the same node was thrown away with it.

**The fix.** Each endpoint now records whether Route/Mount set it (`stub`). `routes()` skips only those endpoints, and only on nodes without subroutes. A method handler registered later overwrites one endpoint and clears its `stub`, so it is reported. The method handlers that stay stubs are still skipped, and nodes with subroutes behave exactly as before.

**Checks I ran:**
- `go test ./...`: `ok github.com/go-chi/chi/v5` and `ok .../middleware`.
- `go vet ./...`: clean.
- `gofmt -l .`: no output.
- `go test -race -run 'Stub|Walk|Routes' -v .`: every test passes, including `TestWalkRouteStubCollision` and `TestRoutesStubCollisionHandlers`.
- `slices` in the tests is fine: `go.mod` says go 1.23 and `tree.go` already imports it.

**Old vs new comparison.** I ran the same probe routers against the HEAD tree and the PR tree, comparing `Walk` output with what `ServeHTTP` actually serves:

| Router | Old `Walk` | New `Walk` | Served |
|---|---|---|---|
| `routeOnly`: `Route("/bar", Get("/"))` | `[GET /bar/]` | `[GET /bar/]` (unchanged) | |
| `plainMountGetStar`: plain `Mount` + `Get("/bar/*")` | every method `/bar/*` | unchanged | |
| `routeEmptyThenGet` | `[]` | `[GET /bar]` | `GET /bar -> 200` |
| `getSlashAfterRoute` | `[GET /bar/x]` | `[GET /bar/ GET /bar/x]` | `GET /bar/ -> 200` |
| `routeThenHandleAll` | `[GET /bar/x]` | every method on `/bar`, plus `GET /bar/x` | `GET /bar -> 200` |

The first two rows show no regression for routers without a collision. Every new entry in the other rows matches a request the router really serves. The test table covers the issue's example, the reverse registration order, `Handle`, plain `Mount`, middleware counts, param and root patterns, and trailing slashes. It follows the table-driven style of the existing `TestWalker` tests.

**One gap remains, and it is not new.** If a handler is registered on the Mount's internal wildcard pattern, e.g. `Route("/bar", …)` followed by `Get("/bar/*", h)`, the probe gives `getStarOnMount [GET /bar/x]` on both old and new trees, while `GET /bar/zzz -> 200 "h"`. `Walk` recurses into the subrouter and ignores that node's own handler. It's a different code path, so I've listed it as a nit for a follow-up rather than a blocker.

My scratch directory is deleted and `git status` is unchanged (`M tree.go`, `M tree_test.go`).
